title: He focuses on the two billion he kept
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When you lose a lot, do you count what you lost or what you kept?

groups.heading: He doesn't focus on the eight billion dollars he lost

lines.text: He starts another business at sixty-five, Jose said. What a guy. Jose read the author's line about his plans.

As Jose reads it, the author said he had no plans to retire yet. Part of his plan B was to make sure that if he left the company he had a business to work in, in addition to his philanthropy. He gives a tribute to a longtime friend who had died, and he makes fun of a health scare with his heart. He doesn't dwell on it.
I still thought I had plenty of time and energy left.

groups.heading: He focuses on the two billion he kept

lines.text: He doesn't focus on the eight billion dollars he lost, Jose said. He focuses on the two billion he kept. What an attitude. This man does not go down.
I'm sure on his deathbed he's going to say something like: I had a great ride, Jose said. That goes to show an element of success is being grateful for every day.
What do you count when you take stock: what you lost, or what you kept?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the biggest loss you have had.
Write what you are grateful for today.
Write what you would start at sixty-five, or any age, that you could start now.
Write your plan B, and how it keeps you working at what you care about.

check.q: What did Jose say the author focuses on?
What did Jose say an element of success is?
What did Jose say the author started at sixty-five?

recap: Count what you kept, and be grateful for every day.
